key_insight: Within binary CSS hypergraph product codes, the simplex-repetition family is essentially the unique qLDPC family that can realize phantom-code logical entangling via physical qubit permutations and Pauli-frame updates.
engineering_relevance: This points to a low-overhead path for fault-tolerant logical CNOTs and circuit reduction, especially for reconfigurable neutral-atom hardware that can support nonlocal qLDPC operations.
method: Prove a deterministic classification of HGP codes satisfying the phantom condition.
Evaluate the resulting codes under circuit-level noise for logical GHZ preparation and Trotterized many-body simulation.
Compare performance against rotated surface-code baselines.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the codes preserve low-weight stabilizer checks and show concrete advantages over rotated surface-code baselines in both benchmarked tasks.
watch_item: The result is constrained to the simplex-repetition HGP family, so broader asymptotic parameter improvements for phantom qLDPC codes remain an open design challenge.
paper_title: Logical Entangling with Phantom Codes in Hypergraph Products
